name: Henge
description: Emulate macOS on iOS and iPadOS
readmeHtml:
Henge

macOS on your iPhone and iPad.

Install · How it works · Website · Releases

Download macOS, install it on the device, and use it.

  • Own emulator — iOS gives apps no hypervisor, so Henge runs the Mac's arm64 code through its own JIT, with its own MMU and devices. It doesn't use QEMU or Virtualization.framework.
  • Installs on the device — Henge downloads Apple's restore image and restores it the way a Mac does. No Mac needed, and nothing is decrypted or patched.
  • Graphics — macOS draws through a virtual GPU, and Henge replays its commands with Metal. Safari and Electron apps like Discord draw on it.
  • Touch — The screen is a trackpad: hold to drag, two fingers to scroll. Esc, Tab, Control, Option and Command sit above the keyboard.
  • Keyboard and mouse — On iPad, a Magic Keyboard or a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse drive the Mac directly.
  • External display — During a Mac session, connect a display with a video-capable USB-C cable or a USB-C/HDMI dock. The mode activates automatically: the monitor shows the Mac, while the iPhone or iPad keeps its trackpad and keyboard controls. Disconnect to return the image to the device. The existing guest resolution is preserved. On iOS 17–26 the same happens through an older iOS route, not yet tried on hardware; outside a Mac session the display mirrors the device. USB-C video is user-confirmed on an iPhone 17 Pro running iOS 27 (development build 0.1/2).
  • Sharing — Copy and paste between macOS and the device, and a shared folder that shows up in Files and on the Mac.
  • Fits the screen — On iPad, a new Mac gets a screen the shape of the iPad's, so there are no black bars.

On an iPhone 17 Pro, macOS reaches the lock screen in about 15 seconds. Discord installs, opens in about 15 seconds, logs in and sends messages.

Install

Sideload Henge.ipa from Releases with SideStore or AltStore, or install Henge.tipa with TrollStore or TrollStore Lite. iOS or iPadOS 17 or later, on an A14 or M1 chip or newer. So far it's tested only on an iPhone 17 Pro: iPad support is new and hasn't run on a real iPad yet.

  • JIT is required: StikDebug, TrollStore (which stops at iOS 17.0), TrollStore Lite (which needs a jailbreak), a jailbreak on its own, or the StikJIT helper built into Henge (iOS 26 or later).
  • Storage: about 43 GB free for macOS Sequoia. That's 17 GB for the download, which you can delete afterwards, and 26 GB for the Mac.
  • Memory: a Mac gets 4, 6 or 8 GB. Sign Henge with the increased memory limit entitlement if your certificate has it.

Then open the Install tab, pick macOS Sequoia 15.6.1, and keep Henge open with the device plugged in. Tahoe 26.6.2 and macOS 27.2 are offered too, but they aren't tested yet.

Sharing with the Mac

Do this once for each Mac: open Terminal on the Mac, then in Henge open Details and tap Type the Set Up Command. Press Return on the Mac, and choose Allow when macOS asks about henge-agent and local networks. It needs the Mac's keyboard layout to be U.S.

Then a Henge folder in the Mac's home folder is the same folder as Files › Henge › Shared. What you copy on the Mac is copied on the device too, and the paste button pastes from the device into the Mac.

Known limits

  • Signing in to an Apple Account inside macOS fails with a verification error.
  • Graphics are tested on macOS's own apps, Chrome, Firefox, VS Code and Discord. Other apps may draw wrongly.
  • For the first few minutes after you log in, macOS is busy starting up in the background, so apps open more slowly.
  • Only one Mac can start per launch. Quit Henge and open it again to start another, and to start one again after restarting or shutting down macOS.
  • iPadOS keeps some keyboard shortcuts for itself, such as Command-Tab.
  • It's emulation, so it runs slower than a real Mac.

Screenshots

Captured on a Mac: the app's own screens with sample data, at iPad and iPhone sizes, showing a frame from Henge's renderer.

Building

To use Henge, install the latest release. Every change lands on main as it's made, so main can be unfinished between releases.

On a Mac with Xcode 27 or later and xcodegen. Henge takes StikJIT, on-device pairing, libslirp and glib from a built Husk checkout at ~/Documents/Coding/Husk (set HUSK to use another path):

ios/scripts/fetch_deps.sh
tools/build_ios_restore.sh
make ios-lib
ios/scripts/package_ipa.sh

That produces ~/Desktop/Henge.ipa, and package_ipa.sh --trollstore writes Henge.tipa.

make builds the engine for the Mac, build/hengevm, and make test runs its tests.

Licence

GPL-2.0-or-later. Henge compiles in usbmuxd (GPLv2 or GPLv3) and code from Husk (GPL-2.0-or-later), so the shipped binary is a combined GPL work. It cannot go on the App Store. See docs/licensing.md.

macOS and the Mac's boot ROM are Apple's and aren't part of Henge. Henge downloads both from Apple when you install.

releases.body:
## What's new?
- macOS 27 (Golden Gate) installs and runs, as well as macOS Sequoia
- Choose your Mac's memory, anywhere from 1 to 16 GB
- Put the Mac on an external display over USB-C, on iOS 27 and on iOS 17-26
- A bit faster: guest memory lookups were reworked, and macOS 27's constant TLB flushes no longer wipe every app's entries
- Settings > Performance: refresh rate (60 Hz, or 120 Hz with ProMotion), faster disk writes, quicker wake from idle, superblocks (experimental) and a 1 GB or 1.5 GB code cache (experimental)
- Colours fixed: macOS no longer looks washed out, and the iPad's P3 screen is colour matched
- iPad: Retina and Performance screen modes, smoother Magic Keyboard scrolling, a smaller and sharper pointer with a size setting, and iPadOS's hide-keyboard key works
- The Mac fills squarer iPhones edge to edge
- Hide the session controls; a three-finger tap brings them back
- JIT: turn it on from the Install tab before your first Mac, LocalDevVPN connects first when it's off, and JIT on cellular says what's wrong and retries (#22, #23)
- Free (personal) Apple developer teams can sign the app
- iPadOS 17 no longer crashes when Metal can't load one of macOS's GPU program

## What's new?
The first release of Henge: macOS on your iPhone and iPad, installed right on the device with no Mac needed.

## Confirmed Working
macOS Sequoia 15.6.1 - installs and boots on an iPhone 17 Pro, lock screen in about 15 seconds
Safari
Discord - install, log in, send messages
Clipboard and file sharing between the iPhone and macOS

iPad support is new and hasn't run on a real iPad yet.

## Installation
Sideload Henge.ipa with SideStore or AltStore, or install Henge.tipa with TrollStore or TrollStore Lite. Enable JIT, open the Install tab and install macOS. Needs iOS 17 or later, an A14 or M1 chip or newer, and about 43 GB free.

## Issues
If any bugs / issues occur, report it to the GitHub or in my Discord Server.

Links:
Discord Server: https://itslevii.dev/discord
Email: hello@itslevii.dev

aiSummary.oneLiner: Cross-platform toolkit for building modular desktop applications.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Henge provides a framework for assembling desktop applications from independent, reusable modules. It abstracts OS-level APIs, allowing developers to write business logic once and deploy it across Windows, macOS, and Linux. The toolkit uses web technologies for the UI layer while providing native system access via a secure bridge. It emphasizes a plugin architecture, where features can be added or removed dynamically. Henge aims to reduce the boilerplate required for modern desktop development.
keyFeatures: Plugin architecture: structures applications as collections of dynamically loaded modules.
Cross-platform API: provides a unified interface for file system, windowing, and OS notifications.
Secure bridge: isolates the web UI from native system access using strict permissions.
Hot reloading: supports rapid UI iteration without recompiling the native host.
Automated builds: includes tooling to package and distribute applications for multiple OSs.

useCases.title: Modular Tools
useCases.description: Build internal company tools where departments only load the modules they need.

useCases.title: Cross-Platform Utilities
useCases.description: Develop system utilities that work consistently across different operating systems.

useCases.title: Extensible Applications
useCases.description: Create software that supports community-built plugins and extensions.

useCases.title: Rapid Prototyping
useCases.description: Quickly prototype desktop apps using familiar web technologies.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Desktop application developers looking for a modular alternative to Electron or Tauri. It requires knowledge of web frontend frameworks and basic system architecture.
